messages:
alex: Quick brain-dump — I'm prototyping a circuit-orchestrator service to centralize canary/A-B fallback decisions across clusters. Goal: consistent safety heuristics + minimal cross-region churn. Thoughts?

maria: high level goal sounds good. main risks i see: signal fidelity across regions and ownership of the final decision (who’s allowed to flip). :thinking:

tj: agree. also need to tie decisions to SLOs+token budgets, not just error spikes. small blip -> don't flip everything.

kevin: interface question — will orchestrator be a central API that returns a routing decision, or a policy bundle pushed to edge routers?

alex: thinking hybrid. primary API for human/ops controls and audits, policy bundles pushed to local proxies for fast path. centralization for observability + appeals.

sam: how do we avoid cascades when one region triggers fallback and others follow? need locality-first rules and a global cooldown.

irene: session affinity & cache-warmup matter. if we fallback to quantized model, cold KV cache may blow latency. we should include a priming probe step before full swap.

kevin: state machine? OPEN / CLOSED / PROBING / SCALEDOWN? we should be explicit about transitions and timeouts.

tj: propose metrics for triggers: p95 latency vs budget, tail latency slope, error-rate rolling window, and synthetic probe failure. combine by weighted score.

alex: rough config prototype: 
```
{
  "circuit_orchestrator": {
    "evaluation_window_sec": "60",
    "latency_p95_ms": "300",
    "error_rate_pct": "2",
    "token_budget_per_tenant": "1000000",
    "fallback_chain": ["local-cache","quantized-128","regional-fallback"],
    "probe_rate": "0.05"
  }
}
```

maria: looks reasonable. we should add a margin factor per-tenant and per-route. some customers care more about correctness than latency.

sam: +1 on per-route weighting. also add hysteresis: require sustained violation for N windows or progressive weight shift (10% increments).

ops-bot: note: canary-monitor reported a 4% 1m error spike in eu-west yesterday at 03:12 UTC.

deply-bot: (typo) deploy-bot: canary rollout for model-v3 started in eu-west at 2026-03-20T03:20:12Z

irene: second thought on probes — do both dry-run inference probes (no billing) and small-sampled live traffic probes to catch semantic regressions. need guardrails to avoid noisy probes impacting latencies.

tj: decision math idea: compute a normalized risk score between 0-100 combining latency, error, semantic diff. thresholds: <30 keep, 30-60 probe, >60 fallback. smoothing with EWMA.

kevin: important: provide a canary pin/escape hatch API so SREs can pin traffic to last-known-good for a given tenant/route instantly. Ops playbook needs that first button.

alex: agreed — add manual override + audit log + automated rollback heuristics. Also want automated gradual downgrade chain rather than all-or-nothing: e.g., first divert 5% to fallback path, observe, then scale.

maria: observability checklist: per-tenant tokens consumed, per-route latency histogram, probe success ratio, last rollback reason, orchestrator decision timeline.

sam: runtime performance note — the orchestrator should avoid per-request RPCs. local proxies should cache decisions with TTL and subscribe to invalidations. central only for policy changes and audits.

irene: also consider model-variant compatibility matrix. some fallbacks not semantically compatible (e.g., reranker -> embedder). orchestrator needs to know safe substitutions per-route.

alex: action items: I’ll draft an RFC with: signal set, state machine, policy bundle format, API surface, observability/alerts, and runbook. can we sync tomorrow 9am PT to walk it?

maria: i can join. also cc @kevin for the proxy push details. :thumbsup:

tj: will prototype weighted scoring util and share sample telemetry queries.

sam: i’ll draft the local TTL/invalidation contract for proxies.

irene: i’ll write probe design (dry-run vs sampled) and priming flow.

alex: thanks all. will post RFC link here when ready.
